questions.q: Why does the top of the Executive Summary page use card visuals instead of a table?
options: Tables are not supported in Power BI Desktop
An executive needs the headline number in the first five seconds, and a card shows one number with nothing to hunt for, unlike a table
Card visuals use less memory than tables
Cards are required before any measure can be created
questions.explain: A card visual shows one number, one label — exactly the instant readability an executive walking into a meeting needs, which a table doesn't provide as directly.

questions.q: Why does selecting a quarter in the page's slicer update every card and chart on the page at once?
options: Because each visual has its own independent copy of the data
Because every measure reads from FactProductSales, which is related to DimDate through the relationship built in Lesson 11, so one slicer selection cross-filters everything connected through it
Because Power BI refreshes the entire file from the warehouse on every click
It's a coincidence specific to card visuals only
questions.explain: Cross-filtering through the model's relationships is the real payoff of building the star schema's relationships correctly before adding any visuals.

questions.q: What does the monthly Total Sales trend line give an Executive that a single card number cannot?
options: A more precise decimal value
Context for whether this quarter's number is part of a trend or a one-off blip, instead of an isolated figure with nothing to compare it against
The ability to export data to Excel
A breakdown by sales reason
questions.explain: A single total invites unfounded speculation about whether it's good or bad; a trend line over time gives it real context.

questions.q: Why does the Executive Summary page deliberately leave out any territory-level breakdown?
options: Because dw.DimTerritory was never imported into the model
Because that's Lesson 14's job on its own dedicated page — mixing company-wide and regional detail onto one page would leave neither question cleanly answered
Because territory data is considered confidential
Because Power BI cannot filter by territory and quarter simultaneously
questions.explain: Scoping this page to company-wide numbers only, and building regional drill-down separately, keeps each page answering one clear question well.

questions.q: Which dimension and columns build the slicer that drives this entire page?
options: dw.DimCustomer, using PersonID and StoreID
dw.DimProduct, using CategoryName
dw.DimDate, using Quarter and Year
dw.DimTerritory, using TerritoryGroup
questions.explain: A quarter/year slicer built from dw.DimDate filters every visual on the page through the fact table's relationship to the date dimension.
